subject.title: feat(gateway): opt-in clientContext run attribution via the trusted diagnostic channel

question: Should trusted diagnostic exporters receive arbitrary caller-asserted metadata as an opaque bag, and if so, what provenance and authority may exporters assign to it?
rationale: Code review can verify isolation and bounds, but it cannot decide whether a caller-controlled value on a trusted channel is an approved identity/cost-accounting contract or merely untrusted correlation metadata.

options.title: Adopt a run-native asserted envelope
options.body: Allow bounded caller metadata, explicitly label it caller-asserted, and carry it with the authoritative run ID on canonical trusted run/model-call events.

options.title: Limit the surface to typed correlation IDs
options.body: Replace the arbitrary object with a narrow typed correlation identifier and optional schema/version fields to reduce spoofing, cardinality, and long-term API commitments.

options.title: Reject caller attribution in core
options.body: Keep trusted diagnostics derived only from OpenClaw-owned state and require external orchestrators to correlate through an out-of-repository integration layer.

recommendation.title: Adopt a run-native asserted envelope
recommendation.body: Allow bounded caller metadata, explicitly label it caller-asserted, and carry it with the authoritative run ID on canonical trusted run/model-call events.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily affects the diagnostic lifecycle and exporter contract established by recent run-event and OpenTelemetry work.
